newsitem.title: FRANCE: Left tops absolute majority in French count.
newsitem.headline: Left tops absolute majority in French count.

text.p: The combined left won an absolute majority of at least 289 seats in France's parliamentary election on Sunday, according to the official Interior Ministry count.

The Socialists, Communists, Radical Socialists, other left and ecologist Greens passed the half-way mark in the 577-seat National Assembly at 11.24 p.m. (2124 GMT). It was not yet clear whether the non-Communist left would achieve an absolute majority on its own without the Communist party.

With 522 seats declared, the Socialist party had 229, the Communists 30, Radical Socialists and other left 27 and the ecologists five. The centre-right had 232 seats and the extreme-right National Front one.
The last results to be declared were from seats in French Caribbean and South American territories, expected to report early on Monday morning, Paris time.
The outgoing centre-right RPR-UDF coalition held a massive 464 seats in the Assembly.
